owner_rules: Done means ALL evidence: implemented as specified (task id), a test that FAILED before and passes now, suites green, measured number vs target, docs regenerated, committed AND pushed to the contract's branch.
Never defer: no "later", "follow-up", "out of scope". If blocked: what blocks, what you tried, what you need; then continue with the next task.
Root cause, then fix: file:line + mechanism. No weakening tests, raising timeouts, skips, relaxed assertions.
No silent scope cuts: never lower targets, caps or test sizes without owner approval.
Never bypass guards: no --no-verify, no bypass env vars, no skip flags.
Deliver continuously: one task per commit, pushed to the contract's branch as it goes green.
Honest reporting: TASK-ID | status | commit | tests | measured vs target | missing.

tasks.title: SO-F-04A Composition of the checks on the Admission external hook: one synchronous function of the shape the hook takes that runs the relationship check of SO-F-04, any other local check and the service checks of SO-F-08 in the order given, honours a degraded answer only from a service check, lets a refusal beat a degraded answer, never lets a degraded answer admit, and adds nothing to the steps or events of the Admission
requirements: composeExternal(...entries), exported from src/engine/federation/admission.mjs, returns one synchronous function of the shape the external option of Admission takes, and runs the checks in the order given; an entry is a function or { check, mayDegrade: true }; anything else, and one array of entries, is a TypeError when the composition is made, and each entry is read once then; nothing else in admission.mjs changes (this one form, entries as arguments, is the signature everywhere in this contract)

the first refusal is the answer and no later check is called; a throw (code external_check_failed, a fixed reason that never repeats the message), a returned promise or thenable (code external_check_async, its rejection caught), a value that is not an object and any answer other than { ok: true } or a degraded answer is a refusal, and a refusal with no code gets external_refused and one with no reason the reason 'an external check refused it' (the fixed reasons are the ones composeExternal writes; the reason a check gives passes through, cut at 160 characters); a pass with extra keys is a pass and the keys are not copied

a degraded answer ({ ok: false, degraded: true }) is honoured only from an entry marked { check, mayDegrade: true }; from any other entry, and as { ok: true, degraded: true } from any check, it is a refusal with the code external_degraded_refused; a degraded answer that gives no code gets external_degraded and one that gives no reason the reason 'a service check could not decide'

after a degraded answer the later checks still run, only to collect reasons; the answer carries ok, degraded (only when degraded), code, reason, position (zero-based) and reasons ({ position, degraded, code, reason } for each degraded answer collected and for the refusal, if any), and never a key of a check's own answer; a refusal beats a degraded answer whatever the order, and with no refusal the first degraded answer is the answer

a degraded answer never contributes to an admit: one degraded check with every other check passing is a denial, at the composition and in an Admission, whichever position it has; the answer is ok true only when every check passed; the Admission appends no federation.admitted and nothing of the payload, and how it records a degraded denial is interim until SO-F-08

an empty list passes, and an Admission given it appends the same events as an Admission with no external option; relationshipGate of SO-F-04, a stand-in for the eligibility gate of PG-W-21B and a stand-in service check compose with no change to the steps, codes or events of the Admission, and a pass skips no later step

no module under src/engine/federation reaches the network or starts a process (child_process, net, tls, http, https, http2, dgram, dns, fetch, a dynamic import()), and the text of the body of composeExternal (Function.prototype.toString), matched by whole words, names no timer, clock, wait or store: a scan of that one function body, which a helper at module level or a computed name does not reveal, so it is one check beside the scan of the modules and the review, and not the proof of 'no wait'

docs/FEDERATION.md states the composition rule, that only a service check may answer degraded, that PG-W-21B WP21-03 will cite this composeExternal, that the order (relationship check, eligibility gate, service checks last) is the node's and provisional pending ADR 8, that the hook is synchronous with the service verdict cached by content_hash and a cache miss refused, that a future asynchronous path is a separate admitAsync, and that what SO-F-08 queues runs every step again when released
tasks.description: The Admission of SO-F-03.3 takes one optional check, and two things need it: the relationship check of SO-F-04 and the external admission service of SO-F-08. This contract gives a node a way to hold both without changing the Admission: one function that runs a list of checks and answers in the hook's own shape. It also gives the hook the one answer the service needs and the hook lacks, 'could not decide', allows it to a service check alone, and fixes what it does: it never helps to admit, it fails closed, and the reasons of the checks that ran after it are kept so that a node can say why. It specifies no service, no trust check, no hold, no queue and no transport, and it changes no step of the Admission and not Admission.admit. The named test imports each module of the contract by namespace (import * as ns), never by name, and asserts that the export it needs is a function or a class before it uses it, so that on the base the red run fails on an assertion; the red-green check treats a load error as BLOCKED, not as red.

criteria.statement: composeExternal is a function exported from src/engine/federation/admission.mjs and returns one synchronous function of the shape the Admission external option takes: it runs the checks in the order given and answers with the first refusal (its code and reason, and its position), and a later check is not called; the form is composeExternal(...entries): a function and an object { check, mayDegrade } are the entries, and any other entry, a mayDegrade that is not a boolean and one array of entries (composeExternal([a, b])) are a TypeError when the composition is made, and a later change to an entry object (its check or its mayDegrade) has no effect; a throw is a refusal with the code external_check_failed and the reason 'an external check threw', which does not contain the message of the throw; a returned Promise and a returned thenable (also one whose then throws) are each refused with the code external_check_async, with the reason 'an external check must answer at once, not with a promise', and the rejection of a returned promise is caught, so that no unhandledRejection is raised (the test listens for it across two event-loop turns); a value that is not an object (null, undefined, a string, an array), an object with no ok, ok as a string and { ok: false } with no code are refusals, and each that gives no code or no reason of its own gets the default code external_refused and the default reason 'an external check refused it', while a reason a check does give passes through (cut at 160 characters) and is the only reason that is not fixed text; { ok: true } with extra keys is a pass and the answer holds none of them; an empty list answers { ok: true, reasons: [] }; the test fails by assertion on the base

stop_rules: Stop and post BLOCKED when a criterion cannot pass without weakening a test, skipping a test or relaxing an assertion.
Stop and ask when the work would name a client product, a person, a server or a seat in repository text; the client names live in docs/CLIENTS.md only.
Stop when the work would add a runtime dependency, a model call, a network call at install or start, a second store for project state, or any reporting that is not opt-in and off by default.

Stop and ask when the work would change a step, a code or an event type of the Admission, change Admission.admit or its constructor, edit a file of SO-F-03.3 beyond adding the one export, or define a hold, a queue or how the Admission handles a degraded answer: that is SO-F-08.

Stop and ask when the work would let a degraded answer, or any answer other than every check passing, produce an admit, or would honour a degraded answer from an entry that is not marked { check, mayDegrade: true }; the composition fails closed.

Stop and ask when the work would define a trust record, a trust check or the place of one in the order beyond the provisional order stated here, edit PG-W-21B, or decide any open ADR (ADR 8 above all); PG-W-21B is frozen pending the owner and cites this contract's composeExternal, not the other way round.

Stop and ask when the work would treat an answer of the hook as a judgement of the node's own steps, or let anything queued after a degraded answer skip a step when it is released.

title: SO-F-04A Composition of the checks on the Admission external hook: one synchronous function of the shape the hook takes that runs the relationship check of SO-F-04, any other local check and the service checks of SO-F-08 in the order given, honours a degraded answer only from a service check, lets a refusal beat a degraded answer, never lets a degraded answer admit, and adds nothing to the steps or events of the Admission
request: Follow-up to the signed SO-F-04, written from the open follow-up row 'Two users of the Admission external hook' of docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md (relationshipGate of SO-F-04, pull request #368, and SO-F-08). Unsigned: a delta proposed for red-team review. It does not supersede SO-F-04 or SO-F-08 and does not edit them: SO-F-04 keeps its ten criteria and SO-F-08 keeps its nine, and this contract adds one function and the rules for composing checks. The id has no '.N' suffix because in this repository a '.N' id (SO-F-03.2, SO-F-09.2) is a superseding version; this is an additive follow-up, as SO-W-08C is to SO-W-08B. OWNER DECISIONS (1 Nov 2026, on pull request #374): (1) SO-F-04A owns composeExternal. PG-W-21B WP21-03 will cite SO-F-04A's composeExternal and will not define a second one; PG-W-21B is frozen pending the owner decision on ADR 8 and this contract does not edit it. (2) After a degraded answer the later checks keep running, but only to collect reasons. A degraded check never contributes to an admit: the overall answer is a denial, it fails closed, and the contract defines no hold (what a node does with a degraded denial, such as queueing the contribution, is SO-F-08 and is not specified here). (3) The hook stays synchronous, and nothing changes in the signed SO-F-03.3 Admission.admit: the only change to src/engine/federation/admission.mjs is the added export. RED-TEAM RESPONSE (1 Nov 2026, on pull request #374, in agreement with the owner decisions): (a) Order. The provisional order of the checks on the hook is the relationship check of SO-F-04 (relationshipGate) first, then the eligibility gate of PG-W-21B WP21-03 when it exists, then the service checks of SO-F-08 last, so that the cheap local checks refuse before a service is called. The eligibility gate is a plain check and never returns a degraded answer. The order is marked provisional pending ADR 8, and composeExternal does not impose it: it runs the order it is given. (b) Synchronous, and how a service fits. The adapter of SO-F-08 makes its asynchronous call before admit is called, caches the verdict by content_hash, and a synchronous service check, an entry { check, mayDegrade: true }, reads the cache; a cache miss is a refusal, neither a pass nor a degraded answer. Any future asynchronous admission is a separate method, admitAsync, with no await between the replay check and the append, so that the check of the mark and the append stay one step; it is not specified here, and nothing here makes Admission.admit asynchronous. This is the shape SO-F-08 is asked to meet; this contract builds none of it. (c) A degraded answer is honoured only from an entry marked as a service check ({ check, mayDegrade: true }). A degraded answer from any other check, and { ok: true, degraded: true } from any check, is a refusal. ADR 8 says a trust check that cannot run refuses, so no check but a service check may say 'could not decide'. WHAT A REFUSAL OR A DEGRADED ANSWER DOES NOT SAY: the external step runs before the signature, authority and replay steps, so an answer of the hook is a statement about the hook's checks only and says nothing about whether the node's own steps would pass. What SO-F-08 queues after a degraded answer has therefore not been judged by the node's own rules, and every item SO-F-08 queues must run every step again (format, external, signature, authority and replay) when it is released; no verdict from the time it was queued is reused. MERGE ORDER of the three specs of pull request #374, which touch the same files. Spec pull requests: #374 changes contracts/scope-one/manifest.json, docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md and docs/scope-one/WBS.md the way every spec-only pull request does, by adding rows and, for a superseded contract, two fields, so it and the other open spec pull request that does the same (SO-F-09.3, #373) take a plain merge of main in whichever order they land, keeping both sets of rows; no spec depends on that order.
